items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, do you know where he got his style? I was especially curious because of what Gunther Schiller had to say in his book.

ctx.x: Well, Charlie Dixon wasn't on the trombone play. His main instrument was the tuba. And that got along on the trombone. And both of them, he'd get a tremendous tone. Willie Long also was a fairly good reader. And so was Benny. Benny wasn't a real fast reader, but they were what we call spellers. And you get together with these guys that can read little and you knowing how it should go when you play it for them and they'd get it on you. Well, it wouldn't take long to run these arrangements down and get them. Well,…
Well, do you know where he got his style? I was especially curious because of what Gunther Schiller had to say in his book.

I think, I'm not passing any criticism. I think there's a little misinformation there. Scott Bagby is just one of these natural musicians. And his playing was just a gift to him. And after he played the clarinet and he got into Troy's band, and by doubling their playing was just one of their first-minded families.
